questions.q: According to the European Commission, who does corporate sustainability reporting help?
options: Investors, civil society organisations, consumers and other stakeholders evaluating companies' sustainability performance
questions.explain: Comparable, reliable disclosures let stakeholders judge sustainability performance.
questions.evidence: This helps investors, civil society organisations, consumers and other stakeholders to evaluate the sustainability performance of companies

questions.q: Companies subject to the CSRD must report according to which standards?
questions.explain: The ESRS set out what and how companies disclose under the CSRD.
questions.evidence: Companies subject to the CSRD have to report according to European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS).

questions.q: What is the EU taxonomy for sustainable activities?
options: A ranking of the greenest countries
A classification system defining criteria for economic activities aligned with net zero by 2050 and wider environmental goals
questions.explain: It is a transparency tool that directs investment to activities needed for the transition.
questions.evidence: The taxonomy is a classification system that defines criteria for economic activities that are aligned with a net zero trajectory by 2050 and the broader environmental goals other than climate.

questions.q: UK SRS S1 and UK SRS S2 are UK versions of which standards?
questions.explain: They are endorsed versions of the ISSB's IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards.
questions.evidence: The UK government consulted on the exposure drafts of the UK versions of IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 – respectively called UK SRS S1 and UK SRS S2.

questions.q: What role was the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) created for?
options: To create a global baseline for sustainability reporting
questions.explain: It was announced at COP26 in Glasgow in 2021.
questions.evidence: with the role of creating a global baseline for sustainability reporting.

questions.q: Which standard does the SECR worked example use to calculate emissions?
options: The GHG Reporting Protocol – Corporate Standard
A standard invented by each trust
questions.explain: Several independent standards are recognised; the example uses the GHG Protocol.
questions.evidence: the standard used in the worked example set out below is the GHG Reporting Protocol - Corporate Standard

questions.q: Are organisations expected to hire specialist consultants to meet the SECR requirements in the example guidance?
options: Only if they have more than one building
No — it is not expected; the figures can be calculated in-house
questions.explain: The worked example shows how to calculate the figures yourself.
questions.evidence: It is not expected that academy trusts will need to engage specialist consultants to support the reporting requirements

questions.q: What is the aim of England's resources and waste strategy?
options: To become a world leader in using resources efficiently and reducing the amount of waste created
questions.explain: It favours recovering and regenerating products and materials.
questions.evidence: Our plan is to become a world leader in using resources efficiently and reducing the amount of waste we create as a society.

questions.q: What do the UK Greening Government Commitments require for information technology?
options: That all IT is bought from UK suppliers
That servers run only at night
That government reduces the carbon emissions and waste caused by its IT
questions.explain: Digital services have an environmental footprint that must be reduced.
questions.evidence: The Greening Government Commitments require government to reduce the carbon (CO2) emissions and waste caused by its information technology

questions.q: What does environmental sustainability mean in the Data and AI Ethics Framework?
options: Thinking about the wider impact of your project on people and the planet, and being mindful of the resources you use
questions.explain: Consider it from the start — it shapes choices of tools, suppliers and infrastructure.
questions.evidence: Environmental sustainability means thinking about the wider impact of your project on people and the planet, and being mindful about the resources you use every day.
